article_title: Comparing Clinical Preparedness of Newly Qualified Diagnostic Radiographers Trained With Immersive Virtual Reality vs. Traditional Simulation: A Mixed-Methods Study.
citation: Karimi Hossein, Clarke Samantha, Watson Emily. (2025). Comparing Clinical Preparedness of Newly Qualified Diagnostic Radiographers Trained With Immersive Virtual Reality vs. Traditional Simulation: A Mixed‐Methods Study. Journal of Medical Radiation Sciences. https://doi.org/10.1002/jmrs.882
title: X-Ray Pro VR Suite by Virtual Medical Coaching for diagnostic radiography training
description: The X-Ray Pro VR Suite is the immersive virtual reality training platform provided by Virtual Medical Coaching that the VR-trained cohort used in this study. It offers dynamic, interactive clinical environments in which learners practise radiographic tasks, observe how kVp and mAs affect image quality, and receive immediate feedback within scenario-based training. The study used it to deliver the same clinical scenarios and total simulation time as traditional physical simulation for 40 radiographers.
requirements: Mandatory participation in assigned simulation sessions
Identical clinical scenarios and total simulation time across training methods for comparability
constraints: The study evaluated it against traditional simulation in radiography education only; effects in other domains are not reported here
target_learners: Undergraduate diagnostic radiography students at two universities
target_learning_goals: Radiographic technique and image quality decision-making
Confidence and adaptability before clinical placement
examples: Students adjusted exposure factors in VR to simulate film/screen characteristics before post-processing, which the article says enhanced their confidence and decision-making
